summary: Chat/user/message id handling (TDLib int53) is disciplined across src/: they arrive as JSON Numbers and are read with longLongValue and carried in int64_t almost everywhere. No int53 id was found read through intValue/integerValue or stored in NSInteger. The real 64-bit defect class in this codebase is the opposite one: TDLib's JSON interface encodes int64 fields as STRINGS (td_json_client.h:18-19), and two readers accept only NSNumber, so those ids silently become 0.

findings.what: `@"emojiId" : fullType[@"custom_emoji_id"] ?: @(0)` stores the raw JSON value. `custom_emoji_id` is int64 in td_api.tl (stickerFullTypeCustomEmoji), and td_json_client encodes every int64 field as a JSON string, so this key holds an NSString, not the NSNumber the header (TGClient+Forums.h:170) promises. Same raw pass-through at TGClient+Forums.m:86 for `icon[@"custom_emoji_id"]` -> @"iconEmojiId".
findings.failure: TGTopicsViewController.m:57 `TGTopicLongLong` returns `[value isKindOfClass:[NSNumber class]] ? [value longLongValue] : 0`. At TGTopicsViewController.m:1507 it reads @"emojiId" from a -forumTopicDefaultIconsWithCompletion: entry, gets an NSString, and yields 0. That 0 flows through commitCreateWithName:iconEmojiId: / commitEditWithName:changeIcon:iconEmojiId: into TGClient+Forums.m:256 `@"custom_emoji_id" : @(iconEmojiId)` and :283 `@"icon_custom_emoji_id" : @(...)`. Result: the user picks a topic icon emoji in the action sheet and the topic is always created/edited with no custom emoji icon at all, falling back to the colour circle. Silent, never logged.

findings.what: `topic[@"order"] ?: @(0)` passes forumTopic.order straight through. Per td_api.tl:3926 `forumTopic ... order:int64`, so this is a JSON string, while TGClient+Forums.h:45 documents `"order" NSNumber int64 sort order`. TGClient.m:1682-1689 already documents and handles exactly this trap for chatPosition.order ('It is an int64 sent as a string, so it must not be compared as a string').
findings.failure: No caller currently sorts on this key (grep for "order" in TGTopicsViewController.m returns nothing), so there is no live failure today. The next caller that follows the header and does `[topic[@"order"] compare:...]` as NSNumber, or `isEqualToNumber:`, gets either a wrong ordering or an unrecognized-selector crash on the NSString.
findings.fix: Wrap with the same TGForumsInt64 helper: `TGForumsInt64(topic[@"order"]), @"order",` at TGClient+Forums.m:88.

findings.what: `topicId, @"topicId", topicId, @"threadId",` aliases forum_topic_id (int32, td_api.tl:3911) to the key "threadId", which TGClient+Messages.m:13-17 TGMsgTopic feeds into `messageTopicThread message_thread_id:int53` (td_api.tl:2983). TGClient+Forums.h:6-9 itself flags that these are not the same identifier.
findings.failure: TGTopicsViewController.m:1023-1030 reads @"threadId" and assigns it to the chat controller's threadId; sends into that topic build messageTopicThread with a forum_topic_id where a message_thread_id is expected. Not a width truncation (int32 widens cleanly into int53) but a wrong-namespace id: the server resolves it to a different thread or rejects it, so messages sent from a topic land outside the topic.
findings.fix: Not a width bug; noted here because it is the only remaining id-identity problem in this area. The correct construction is `@{@"@type":@"messageTopicForum", @"forum_topic_id":@((int32_t)topicId)}` when the target chat is a forum, versus messageTopicThread for legacy comment threads. Confirm with the forums/messages owner before changing; do not simply widen the type.
